analysis.title: Equities - Tactical Top Picks (Unified Global Markets PMA Equity Sales, 19 Nov 2026)
key_insights: The list has 10 open tactical ideas, all Buy-rated: Accelleron, Prysmian, Rolls-Royce, Barclays, NVIDIA, Netflix, Edwards Lifesciences, Oracle, Boeing and Mitsubishi Heavy. Seven carry the UBS CIO Most Preferred (MP) tag. Netflix, Edwards and Oracle's neighbours aside, Edwards and Netflix are Buy without MP.

New this edition: Accelleron (16 Nov), Prysmian (16 Nov), NVIDIA (16 Nov) and Mitsubishi Heavy (17 Nov) carry the NEW flag. Rolls-Royce (19 Oct), Barclays (14 Sep), Netflix and Edwards (9 Nov) and Oracle (2 Nov) were carried over.

Boeing is marked to be closed at the 19 Nov 2026 closing price. It was entered at 192.72 USD on 5 Oct and now trades at 162.91 USD, -15.5% absolute. That price is below the 163.81 USD lower boundary shown on its page.
Four of the open ideas are below their inception price: Barclays -14.1%, Netflix -6.5%, Oracle -4.5% and NVIDIA -3.3%. Prysmian, Edwards and Rolls-Royce are near flat.

Each idea has an upper and lower level that define the absolute-return boundaries and act as triggers for removing it. For beta below 0.8 the bands are 9% down and 12% up. For beta 0.8 to 1.2 they are 12% down and 16% up. For beta above 1.2 they are 15% down and 20% up. The upper level drops to the price target if the target falls below it.

NVIDIA: UBS says Nvidia could deliver above-consensus Q3 earnings (dated 17.11.26), supported by supply-constrained AI demand. September Taiwan exports surged above seasonality. Semiconductor valuations have derated sharply despite accelerating AI demand. A CEO change is not expected to affect the long-term product roadmap. This one-pager was finalized 16 Nov, before the print.

Accelleron: strong marine demand backed by Chinese new-build activity and fully booked regional shipyards. Marine capex is expected to grow about 15% in 2027. UBS cites a data-center gas-engine tailwind where Accelleron holds more than 80% share. Equipment growth pressures near-term mix, and installed units should lift service margins around 2030.

Prysmian: UBS expects 2027 earnings upgrades from fibre pricing (about 25% of contracts still await repricing), Digital Solutions growth, and data-center-driven Electrification growth. Transmission margins are seen rising to 24-25% by 2030 from 20-21%. Catalysts are two more hyperscaler fibre agreements and a Q2 2027 capital markets day.

Rolls-Royce: UBS calls the turnaround incomplete and expects further earnings upgrades. FY26 results around 23 Feb 2027 may bring higher medium-term cash flow guidance. Civil Aerospace margins are forecast to approach top peers and Defence profitability to exceed most peers. Power Systems gains from data-center backup demand.

Barclays: thesis rests on investment banking revenue momentum, structural hedge earnings, cost actions and capital returns. UBS views it as undervalued versus peers on a 2026 P/E of 6.58. The stock trades at 4.111 GBP, close to the 4.08 GBP lower level.
Edwards Lifesciences: strong Q3 and TAVR growth. The PROGRESS trial widens the addressable market. Investor Day on 4 December 2026 should highlight moderate aortic stenosis and pipeline innovation.

Netflix: Q3 revenue was in line and profit ahead, but near-term trends are softer. UBS sees advertising monetization upside and says estimates are moderating while long-term upside remains intact. The stock is 6.5% below inception and near the 56.28 USD lower level.

Oracle: the one-pager lists a 250 USD target against a 113.89 USD price. Growth is tied to data-center capacity for cloud demand. The page's investment-case bullets are Boeing's text repeated, not Oracle's.

Mitsubishi Heavy: energy systems earnings are entering an expansion phase led by gas turbine profit. UBS raised its target to JPY 5,240 and reiterated Buy on 12 Nov. A JPY 300bn buyback covers 3.6% of shares.

Track record of closed ideas, 2026 YTD (86 ideas): Switzerland +7.2% absolute and +3.7% relative (14 ideas), Europe -0.4% and -1.7% (30), Americas -1.0% and -2.1% (32), Asia-Pacific -5.7% and -4.1% (10). Since inception across 278 ideas the average is +1.2% absolute and +0.2% relative, with an average life of 39 trading days.

earnings_insights: NVIDIA: UBS says Q3 earnings (dated 17.11.26) could come in above consensus. This is a forecast made in a one-pager finalized 16 Nov, before the print. No reported figures are given.
Netflix: Q3 revenue was in line and profit ahead of expectations per UBS. No EPS or revenue figures are stated.
Edwards Lifesciences: UBS cites strong Q3 results across key franchises. No figures are stated. Investor Day is 4 December 2026.
Rolls-Royce: FY26 results are expected around 23 Feb 2027, with potential for higher medium-term cash flow guidance and a guidance upgrade.
Prysmian: 3Q conference call (29 Oct, per UBS source note) offered line of sight on 2027 upgrades. A capital markets day is expected in Q2 2027.

Boeing: UBS source note says charges on major development programs have left a 0% YTD adjusted EBIT margin, which could decline further. Free cash flow is forecast to rise from USD 2.2bn in 2026 to USD 15.1bn by 2030.

risk_factors: Boeing breached its lower boundary and is being closed at a 15.5% loss from entry.
Barclays (4.111 vs 4.08 GBP) and Netflix (59.82 vs 56.28 USD) sit close to their lower levels.
Accelleron: a cyclical downturn in marine investment, FX translation, regional regulation and raw material costs.
Prysmian: grid margins falling below the 2027 forecast, slower Transmission growth to 2028, US price competition at Encore Wire.
Rolls-Royce: forecasts depend on air traffic, national defence spending and exchange rates.
NVIDIA: competition from AMD and Intel and the link between semiconductor revenue and corporate profitability.
Edwards: competitive device launches, pricing pressure, trial delays, hospital capacity limits.
Oracle: execution risk from the sales reorganization and slipped deals.
Mitsubishi Heavy: capex weakness in Japan, Europe, US and China, input cost increases and competition.
